Subject: So this happened: Fernhollow Photo is official

Okay, family update: Fernhollow Photo is a real business now!!

I filed the LLC on October 22 on my lunch break, sitting in the car outside Fred Meyer. I cried a little, which was probably a weird thing to do in a Fred Meyer parking lot, but here we are. The website went live November 1, and I’ve been staring at it like it might suddenly tell me I made this all up.

I’ve been thinking about doing this for two years. Not in a “quit my job tomorrow and hope the universe sends me clients” way. More in a “quietly plan it in my head for ages, learn everything I can, and then still get emotional next to the grocery carts” way.

Some of you know Rosebud Lane is closing at the end of October. I shot weddings for Marisol for four years, and I learned so much from her. She gave me the kind of experience you can’t get from watching a tutorial: how to stay calm when the timeline goes sideways, how to notice the little moments, and how to keep moving when your feet are telling you to lie down in a field. She’s been incredibly generous in sending couples my way, and I’m grateful. Marisol, thank you for teaching me so much and for trusting me with people who matter to you.

So far, I have 14 weddings booked for 2027. Six came through Marisol, and eight found me on my own. I’m excited about every one of them, but I have to tell you about the first booking that was 100% mine: Dahlia and Ken, at Timberline on June 12. They found me through the Multnomah Falls couple photos I took, and they said they loved them. I may have reread that email several times. Possibly while making an extremely dignified noise that Pickle found concerning.

For the bigger weddings, Jae will second shoot with me. They’ll be paid per wedding, and having someone I trust there with another camera and another set of eyes makes me feel a lot better. I’ve also got health insurance figured out: I picked a marketplace plan, and it starts January 1. Dad, I know this is one of the first things you’re going to ask, so yes, it’s sorted. I’m not winging the whole grown-up part, even if the LLC paperwork happened in a car.

The name has a little family history in it, too. Fernhollow is from the fern hollow trail behind Grandma’s old place in Gresham. That’s where I took my first real pictures with her Pentax. Grandma, this is for you. I still remember how it felt to have that camera in my hands and to look at familiar things like they were worth stopping for. I guess I’ve been doing that ever since.

Sam celebrated by making a cake that said FERNHOLOW. One L short, but absolutely correct in spirit. We ate it anyway. It was delicious and probably the most official cake a new business has ever had.

I’m nervous, obviously. Starting something of your own is a lot, and there are a lot of details to keep track of. But I’m also really happy. I’ve been planning for this, I have weddings on the calendar, I have people in my corner, and I get to make pictures for a living. That’s a pretty wonderful thing to get to say.

Also, Thanksgiving at Ruthie’s is in two weeks! I’ll bring the camera. If anyone wants some free family pictures while we’re all together, tell me and I’ll make time for it. No pressure and no matching-outfit requirements. (Unless Uncle Greg is already coordinating everyone. In that case, I respect the commitment.)

Love you all. I’m excited to tell you this, and even more excited to see everybody soon.
